A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, figures, equations, table, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v4 reports original geometric-shape simulations, bird-classification and pneumonia-detection experiments, classifier accuracies, and causal edge-stability results.

after.justification: v5 reports these original empirical studies, including revised bird edge-stability results and newly disclosed fitted regression coefficients.

M1.justification: The proposed FCI/PAG approach using macro-level features and predicted labels retains the same background-knowledge constraints. The HydraNet heads, weighted loss, logistic classifier, and ResNet18 architecture are retained; the revisions concern settings and parameter disclosure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the geometric-shape simulation, nine-group Caltech-UCSD bird classification, and ChestX-ray8 pneumonia/control classification. Revised sample counts remain within the existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: LIME and SHAP, using Deep Explainer for SHAP, remain the evaluated qualitative comparators on both real-data tasks. Their representative image comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5 and the simulation appendix revise HydraNet pretraining from 10,000 to 2,500 images. Section 6.1 changes bird training from 2,849 to 2,489 images, X-ray data from 239 to 240 images, and X-ray testing from 50 to 55 images. Section 6.2 changes FCI thresholds from 10^-5 to 0.05 for birds and 0.05 to 0.01 for X-rays. These substantially revise reported settings, although the PDFs do not establish whether they reflect reruns or reporting corrections.

E4.justification: The omitted-confounder simulation and qualitative LIME/SHAP case comparisons are retained. No additional ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error analysis is introduced; the changed bird chart reports the existing primary analysis.

E5.justification: The chi-square conditional-independence significance thresholds change in both real-data experiments. Bootstrap counts remain 50 for birds and 100 for X-rays, with the same edge-stability reporting practice and no newly reported uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Figure 8(a) substantially changes the bird stability profile: leading features change from Size, Eye Color, and Bill Shape to Wing Shape, Wing Pattern, and Tail Shape. Size falls from approximately 0.86 to 0.18, while Wing Shape rises from approximately 0.34 to 0.90, under revised reported settings. Figure 8(b) and classifier accuracies remain unchanged. The appendix also adds numerical regression parameters.

T1.justification: The structural causal models, faithfulness assumption, causal-graph reasoning, and Shapley counterexample retain the same mathematical content. The appendix calculations for valid and invalid adjustment sets are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claim that causal structure learning can distinguish possible causal determinants from confounded associations using interpretable macro-level features and black-box predictions.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning spatially overlapping features, background knowledge, weak identifiability, expert annotations, and limitations of automatic feature extraction remain substantively unchanged. The revised bird rankings change reported findings without adding a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly reports the logistic-regression intercept, -1.82530524, and four fitted coefficients with their corresponding shapes. This improves reconstruction of the simulation classifier. Architecture, optimizer details, preprocessing groupings, and software access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an acknowledgment and citation to Kumar et al. (2020) concerning criticisms of Shapley-based feature importance. The broader research positioning is retained; most citation changes reflect conversion to author-year formatting.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited grammatical corrections, updates author affiliation/contact text, changes citation and section-numbering conventions, and organizes the existing appendix material under labeled Appendices A-C. The narrative order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column document with different typography, spacing, and widespread resizing and relocation of figures and equations. Table I becomes a wider, restyled Table 1 with a shortened caption. Figure 8(a) also changes bar ordering and axis scaling.

improvement.justification: v5 fixes the bird split arithmetic and aligns Figure 8's leading features with Figure 9's caption and the retained wing-feature discussion, which were inconsistent in v4. Appendix B adds fitted classifier parameters. These provide limited gains in consistency and reproducibility; the revised settings and results do not establish stronger empirical validation.
